messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — ran the new latent-consistency batch probe on glue-embed-25k with specter-lite fp16 -> int4 path. recall@10 dropped ~4.2% vs fp16.
Oliver: Yikes. Was that per-channel int4 or per-tensor symmetric?
Tess: It was per-tensor symmetric using the default quant pipeline. Command I ran: `python quantize.py --model /models/specter-lite --bits 4 --mode symmetric`
Sam: Thanks. Can you paste the exact eval command and seed? want to repro locally.
Maya: Eval command: `python eval_embeddings.py --data data/glue-25k --model /runs/specter-lite/int4 --knn 10 --metric recall --sim cosine --seed 42 --batch 512 --microbatch 128`
Oliver: Two quick guesses: (1) quantization clipping too aggressive -> centroid shift, (2) similarity metric sensitivity. Did you try dot-product?
Maya: Only cosine so far. No whitening or post-hoc re-scaling.
Tess: We saw centroid drift on a previous compact model. Try per-channel quant + percentile clipping. E.g.: `python quantize.py --mode per_channel --clip 0.995`
Sam: Also try calibration with a held-out 5k set (not in glue-25k train split). Re-calibrating scales helps align norms.
Maya: Will run per-channel + clip0.995 and calibration. Spawning jobs now.
embed-bot: Job queued: eval-98321 (per-channel int4, clip=0.995, calib=5k). ETA ~18m.
Oliver: When you have results, run quick UMAP of fp16 vs int4 to visually check cluster collapse. `umap --n_neighbors 15 --min_dist 0.1` — color by class.
Tess: Also compute silhouette score + mean pairwise intra/inter cluster cos diff. Short script: `scripts/cluster_metrics.py --preds preds.pkl`
Maya: Early logs from the per-tensor symmetric job (fp16 vs int4):
```
SUMMARY: recall@1: fp16=0.412, int4=0.381
recall@10: fp16=0.732, int4=0.688
silhouette: fp16=0.21, int4=0.13
mean-intra-cos: fp16=0.67, int4=0.59
```
Maya: Per-channel run still running but looking better in first 1k samples.
Sam: If per-channel improves, that's a good sign. If not, try asymmetric quant and narrower clip (0.999 -> less clipping) and post-quant rescale by median norm.
Tess: We should also check knn stability: run `knn --k 10 --seed 123 --repeats 5` to measure nondeterminism from microbatching. microbatch=128 might introduce small differences.
Oliver: Good call. Microbatching affects accumulation order and float rounding — for int4 those tiny diffs can move nearest neighbors. Try microbatch 64 / 256 to see sensitivity.
Maya: Noted. I'll queue microbatch sweep after per-channel finishes.
embed-bot: Job update: eval-98321 (per-channel) completed — job_id 98321a. results uploaded to /runs/specter-lite/int4/per-channel/98321a/results.json
Maya: Per-channel results (quick): recall@10 jumped to 0.716, silhouette=0.18. Still ~1.6% down vs fp16 but a lot better.
Sam: Nice. Can you run a tiny re-scale experiment: divide int4 vectors by median_norm_fp16 / median_norm_int4 and re-eval? Should be quick and tells if global norm mismatch is main culprit.
Tess: If that closes gap, add a tiny calibration step into the quant pipeline. If not, we might need small retrain-aware quant or l2-per-channel pre-scaling.
Maya: I'll run median-norm rescale next and post numbers here. ETA ~10m.
Oliver: Also dump a few misretrieved cases for manual inspection (queries with large embedding-norm changes). paste one example here when you have it.
Maya: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam: If median-rescale helps, we can add it as a fallback in Optimize recommendations for int4 onboardings.
Tess: Agreed. Document the commands + config so SEs can reproduce. I'll add a short doc in the run's artifacts.
Maya: Uploading misretrieval examples and scripts now. Linking when complete.
embed-bot: Artifact uploaded: /runs/specter-lite/int4/per-channel/98321a/artifacts/misretrievals.tar.gz
Maya: Done — microbatch sweep queued (64,128,256), median-rescale run queued, and the knn-stability repeats. Will report a final mini-summary once all jobs finish.
Oliver: Sweet. If anything still weird after rescale, ping me and I'll try asymmetric per-channel plus per-layer clipping.
Maya: Will do. Closing for now — followups in this thread.
